long_biography.plain_text:
The death of her father brought Anna Angelicoussis into shared responsibility for a Greek maritime enterprise alongside her brother John. Their partnership continued until the siblings divided their commercial interests and pursued independent operations. Anna used that separation to assemble a private platform serving three markets: dry bulk cargoes, petroleum transport and liquefied gas.

That history places her between inheritance and entrepreneurship. A family stake gave her the initial position, but the later portfolio reflects years of separate ownership and development under her direction. It also distinguishes her from the branch led by her niece Maria after John's death. Her economic interest lies in closely held operating companies, whose fleets and balance sheets cannot be read as a statement of her individual assets.

uncertainties.detail: The source record's display name says Mr, but its title says Mrs and its gender says Female. Public sources consistently identify Anna Angelicoussis as a woman, so Mrs Anna Angelicoussis is proposed as a high-confidence correction rather than treating the record as a male namesake.

The subject is Anna Angelicoussis, born in August 1955 and sister of John Angelicoussis. She is not Maria Angelicoussis, John's daughter and the inheritor of his separate group; that distinction is retained only because it is essential to identity and wealth control.

Lloyd's List uses Anna Angelicoussi, while Forbes and the source record use Anna Angelicoussis. The dossier retains the source-record spelling and treats Angelicoussi as an alternative transliteration rather than a different person.

Forbes labels Angelicoussis self-made, but the documented succession to family shipping interests materially predates her independent group. Inherited and expanded more precisely captures both the transferred starting position and her later creation and development of separate businesses.

The existing August 1955 birth month and year align with Forbes. Lower-authority sources supply an exact day and place, but adequate independent corroboration was not found, so birth_day and place_of_birth remain unproposed.

Public sources establish ownership of private shipping companies but do not disclose her exact current stakes, personal balance sheet or the allocation of family holdings. Fleet counts, vessel values, company assets and any business valuation are not treated as personal wealth.
